## Avoid legacy features

Always use runes mode for new code, and avoid features that have more modern replacements:

- use `$state` instead of implicit reactivity (e.g. `let count = 0; count += 1`)
- use `$derived` and `$effect` instead of `$:` assignments and statements (but only use effects when there is no better solution)
- use `$props` instead of `export let`, `$$props` and `$$restProps`
- use `onclick={...}` instead of `on:click={...}`
- use `{#snippet ...}` and `{@render ...}` instead of `<slot>` and `$$slots` and `<svelte:fragment>`
- use `<DynamicComponent>` instead of `<svelte:component this={DynamicComponent}>`
- use `import Self from './ThisComponent.svelte'` and `<Self>` instead of `<svelte:self>`
- use classes with `$state` fields to share reactivity between components, instead of using stores
- use `{@attach ...}` instead of `use:action`
- use clsx-style arrays and objects in `class` attributes, instead of the `class:` directive

### `onevent` attributes are delegated

Event attributes replace event directives: Instead of `on:click={handler}` you write `onclick={handler}`. For backwards compatibility the `on:event` syntax is still supported and behaves the same as in Svelte 4. Some of the `onevent` attributes however are delegated, which means you need to take care to not stop event propagation on those manually, as they then might never reach the listener for this event type at the root.

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
